title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is §3 (manuscript p. 26), 'Étude des sections de E_U dans Γ'. It is the opening of Grothendieck's analysis of the section conjecture in the Longue Marche notes (c. 1981).

Setup. U is a smooth, geometrically connected scheme of finite type over a field K that is finitely generated over Q. A marginal note records that a universal cover Ū of U has been chosen; this fixes K̄, E_K and E_U and the map E_U→E_K. This gives the fundamental exact sequence (1) 1 → π_{U/K}=π_1(U_K̄) → E_U=π_1(U) → E_K=Γ=Gal(K̄/K) → 1, written vertically in the left margin.

The object of study is sections of (1) up to π_{U/K}-conjugacy. Equivalently, these are isomorphism classes of sections of the morphism of classifying topoi B_U → B_K ('Classes d'isomorphie / Sections de B_U sur B_K'). He also considers sections over open subgroups E'_K ⊂ E_K, which amounts to finite extensions K'/K.

First observation. Suppose U embeds in a commutative group scheme (e.g. via the Albanese map into an abelian variety) or in a 'rigid' scheme. Then the Kummer/section map U(K) → {sections of B_U over B_K} / {π-conjugacy classes of sections of (1)} is injective. Rational points give sections via their decomposition groups.

He then announces that he will look for other 'geometric' ways to produce sections. For a curve of type (g,ν) ≠ (0,0),(0,1), i.e. with π_{U/K} ≠ 1, a point at infinity (cusp) i gives an inertia ('groupe de lacets') subgroup L_i ≅ Ẑ(1). The next page continues: its centralizer gives 1 → L_i → Z(L_i) → Γ → 1. Splittings of this extension (for instance from a uniformizer at the cusp) form a torsor under H^1(Γ, Ẑ(1)) ≅ K*^ (the Kummer completion of K*). They map to sections of (1); these are the modern 'cuspidal sections'. A Proposition then says these classes differ from those of rational points, and that distinct cusps give distinct classes in the anabelian case.

The page thus sets up the section conjecture together with the cuspidal-section packets.
errors: No real error on this page. The injectivity of U(K) → sections, for U embedded in a commutative group scheme, implicitly needs A(K) to have no nontrivial divisible elements, i.e. Mordell–Weil/Lang–Néron finite generation for K finitely generated over Q. This is not stated.
The condition on the curve type should read (g,ν) ≠ (0,0),(0,1). The machine transcription 'type (0,0) ou (0,1)' drops the negation, as the next page confirms.
On the next page 'Hom(Γ,T)' with T=Ẑ(1) a nontrivial Γ-module should be H^1(Γ,T) (crossed homomorphisms). The Kummer identification with K*^ is correct for H^1.

ideas.what: Sections of 1→π_1(U_K̄)→π_1(U)→Gal(K̄/K)→1 up to conjugacy, as an object of study for K finitely generated over Q, including sections over open subgroups (finite extensions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings 1983, Esquisse d'un programme 1984)
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983); Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Sections viewed as isomorphism classes of sections of classifying topoi B_U → B_K
ideas.modern_name: Topos-theoretic / gerbe formulation of sections (étale homotopy type)

ideas.what: Injectivity of U(K) → conjugacy classes of sections when U embeds in an abelian variety / commutative group scheme or a 'rigid' scheme
ideas.modern_name: Injectivity part of the section conjecture (via Albanese/Kummer and Mordell–Weil)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings); written up by Nakamura, Mochizuki, Stix

ideas.what: Sections from cusps: inertia L_i ≅ Ẑ(1), its centralizer, and splittings forming a K*^-torsor
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (mentions sections from points at infinity)

missed.claim: Injectivity is stated for U embedding in a 'rigid' scheme as an alternative to a commutative group scheme. This suggests an intended class of 'rigid' targets beyond Albanese embeddings, which is not developed.
missed.quote: Si U se plonge dans un groupe commutatif ou un schéma rigide... l'application U(K) → Sections de B_U sur B_K est injective
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. Injectivity is already known in broad generality (e.g. for hyperbolic curves and subvarieties of abelian varieties), so this adds little.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an early working draft of the section conjecture and of cuspidal sections. Both are well known and credited to Grothendieck, with later detailed treatments by Nakamura and Stix. Nothing here appears to be absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'type (0,0) ou (0,1)' should be read as type ≠ (0,0), (0,1) (i.e. π_1(Ū)=π_{U/K} ≠ {1}).
'en vue [?] un = temps [?] regarder' is likely 'en même temps on regardera'.
'(ce qui signifie que l'on fait une catégorie de base ...)' is likely 'une extension de base K' de type fini sur le corps Q et finie sur K'.
The insertion over the first line reads roughly 'schéma géométriquement connexe lisse de type fini sur le corps K'.

Near the bottom, 'groupe pro-[?] i.e. π̂=π' is uncertain. Context (next page: L_i, Z(L_i)) suggests the passage concerns a point at infinity and its 'groupe de lacets' (inertia) giving a subgroup or semi-direct product with Gal(K̄/K).
'Sections de B_U sur B_K' has the marginal insertion 'Classes d'isomorphie de' above it (classifying topoi B).
